extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: CONTEXTUAL is a dataset for evaluating context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning in large multimodal models. It consists of 506 challenging instructions requiring joint reasoning over embedded text and visual context in images across eight real-world scenarios: time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes, mobile application, webpages, infographics, and miscellaneous natural scenes.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng
extraction.citeAs: Wadhawan, R., Bansal, H., Chang, K.-W., & Peng, N. (2024). CONTEXTUAL: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Text-Rich Visual Reasoning in Large Multimodal Models. Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from six different sources: LAION-5B for Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract categories using keyword search with CLIP-retrieval UI; Rico Dataset for Application Usage category; scraped website links from Open WebText Initiative for Web Usage category; and test sets from existing VQA datasets (InfographicVQA for Infographic category, STVQA and ESTVQA for Miscellaneous Natural Scenes category). Human-written instructions and reference responses were created by authors following specific annotation guidelines requiring context-sensitive reasoning over text and visual elements.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from LAION-5B (using CLIP-retrieval UI with category-specific keywords), Rico Dataset (66,000 UI screens from 9,300 Android apps), Open WebText Initiative (website screenshots), InfographicVQA dataset, STVQA dataset, and ESTVQA dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Stage 1: Images categorized under Time, Shopping, Navigation, and Abstract underwent manual filtering to guarantee suitability for annotation. For Application Usage, Web Usage, Infographic, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes, heuristic-based filtering was performed using PaddleOCR to detect text in images, selecting the top 500 images with the highest number of words. Stage 2: Authors divided into two groups annotated four categories each following strict annotation guidelines. Stage 3: MTurk workers verified correctness of each sample, with 96% found to be correctly annotated. Incorrect samples were filtered out, and each author group reviewed samples created by the other group to ensure adherence to guidelines and filter out low-quality samples, resulting in 506 instances.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-written instructions (questions or imperative tasks) and human-written ground-truth responses were created by authors. Each sample consists of an image, instruction, and response triplet, with the constraint that responding to an instruction accurately requires context-sensitive joint reasoning over textual and visual cues in the image. Instructions were designed to cover diverse types including questions and imperative tasks, with varied complexity (extractive instructions and reasoning-based instructions). Authors followed key collection guidelines ensuring instructions require context-sensitive reasoning and cannot be answered by text-based reasoning over detected OCR alone.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MTurk workers verified the correctness of each sample and found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly. Each author group reviewed the samples created by the other group to ensure adherence to guidelines and filtered out low-quality samples.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Authors from University of California Los Angeles; MTurk workers mainly from the US for human baseline performance and human evaluation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: PaddleOCR (PP-OCRv4 model) for text detection and OCR extraction; ShareGPT-4V-7B for dense image captions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A subset of 100 samples from the 506 will be released as validation set with reference responses, while reference responses for the remaining 406 samples will be kept hidden. The distribution of validation samples closely mirrors the overall dataset distribution (30 samples from Miscellaneous Natural Scenes category and 10 samples from remaining categories).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: During data collection, the authors aimed to ensure that the images, human-written instructions, and reference responses are not offensive to any social group. The authors are aware that existing multimodal models are capable of generating harmful responses despite safeguard filters. The extension of this work can focus on understanding the impact of different social groups on the human baseline performance on the CONTEXTUAL dataset. The authors note that linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses would change with different social groups.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging for modern LMMs while humans excel on it. There is a significant performance gap of 30.8% between GPT-4V (the current best-performing Large Multimodal Model) and human performance. The authors note that human annotators were mainly from the US, and linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses would change with different social groups. The qualitative analysis reveals that models encounter difficulties with precise visual perception and exhibit hallucinations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of large multimodal models' capability on context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning. The dataset is designed to assess the joint reasoning abilities of LMMs over embedded text and visual features in images across diverse natural and digital text-rich visual scenarios. Use cases include evaluating model performance on time reading, shopping, navigation, abstract scenes (memes, quotes), mobile application usage, webpage understanding, infographics interpretation, and miscellaneous natural scenes.
